title: Both Sides, Likely Outcomes & Portfolio Action
web_title: 9. Bull vs. Bear, Portfolio Action & Redeployment Plan
book_title: Chapter 9: Bull vs. Bear, Likely Outcomes & Our Action Plan
question: What should you do with new capital and the existing holding when the business, financing engine, and tape point in different directions?

epigraph.quote: The goal is to double Bitcoin per share in seven years through the use of digital credit.
epigraph.author: Phong Le, President and CEO, Q3 2026 earnings call [4]

web_blocks.html: The evidence supports neither a simple Bitcoin-proxy endorsement nor a claim that the company is already impaired beyond repair. Strategy owns a large and liquid Bitcoin reserve, has access to multiple capital markets, and continues to grow cloud subscriptions. At the same time, the software operation does not yet fund its own obligations; the treasury yield per share was negative year to date through November 9; preferred dividends, repurchases, ATM issuance, and potential Bitcoin sales now form a complex capital-management loop; and the stock is below its major trend averages. Your decision must distinguish the business-quality call, the capital-structure thesis, the market entry, and the actual portfolio holding. [1][2][12][15]

web_blocks.title: The bull case, stated as strongly as the evidence permits

web_blocks.html: The bull case starts with scarce-asset exposure at scale. Strategy held 850,364 BTC as of November 8 and had built a $4.77 billion USD Reserve plus $146.2 million of USD Cash. The company says this reserve system protects dividends and interest while leaving broader cash for Bitcoin purchases, buybacks, and other treasury purposes. Bitcoin itself has a fixed supply schedule, and broader institutional access can expand demand. If Bitcoin appreciates faster than the carrying cost of the capital stack, common equity can benefit from a larger asset base, a manageable preferred burden, and a premium that permits share issuance above asset value. [12][13][14][17]

There is also a plausible software option. Subscription services revenue grew from $106.8 million in FY2024 to $175.7 million in FY2025 and from $46.0 million to $68.6 million in the Q3 year-over-year comparison. Pfizer, Helsana, B&H Photo, and Lotte describe workflow uses in which governed definitions, mobile access, report rationalization, retail operations, or AI agents become embedded in everyday work. If this transition improves retention and recurring gross profit, the software business could become more valuable than its current cash record suggests. [1][2][5][6][7][8][9]

Finally, the capital system can adapt. The November 9 update shows stock proceeds allocated among Bitcoin purchases, STRC repurchases, and USD Cash rather than a one-way accumulation policy. The company has a reserve for fixed-dollar obligations, can adjust preferred dividend terms subject to its own policies, and has authorized common-stock and preferred repurchases. A capital structure that changes its mix in response to market conditions could reduce pressure on common shareholders in a downturn and preserve optionality for a later upswing. Management argues that digital credit broadens the investor base and enables a different financing channel. [12][13][16][17]

web_blocks.title: The bear case is a mechanism failure, not a Bitcoin-price prediction

web_blocks.html: The most direct bear evidence is the company’s own operating disclosure. FY2025 software operations did not generate positive cash flow from operations, and management did not expect the software business to generate enough cash to satisfy obligations or liquidity needs over the following twelve months. Cloud growth is real, but support and license revenue were lower in the Q3 comparison and on-premises support reaches its full sunset at year-end 2026. The software business is not yet an internal cash engine capable of carrying the preferred dividend and interest stack. [1][2]

The second weakness is per-share dilution. Management’s goal is to double Bitcoin per share, but the company ledger showed BTC Yield of −4.2% year to date through November 9. Gross Bitcoin holdings reached 850,364, yet the management-defined per-share metric fell. In the week ended November 8, Strategy sold 2.05 million MSTR shares for $283.8 million net proceeds; only $81.9 million funded 1,036 BTC, while $188.3 million funded STRC repurchases and $13.6 million went to USD Cash. This may still strengthen the balance sheet, but it does not support a claim that all equity issuance directly increases BTC per share. [12][15]

The third weakness is a feedback loop. If Bitcoin falls, the reserve value falls; if the market premium compresses, equity issuance becomes less accretive or unavailable; if issuance slows, Bitcoin buying may slow; and preferred dividend obligations continue to be dollar-denominated. The USD Reserve reduces the risk of a forced sale but is not infinite and the preferred claims are not secured by Bitcoin. Management has publicly authorized Bitcoin monetization when advantageous, including for dividends and security repurchases, so the old “never sell” slogan is no longer a safe assumption. [3][12][16][17]

The fourth weakness is the residual nature of common equity. Our approximate $107 common residual value per share is only an asset-based anchor; it assumes updated Bitcoin holdings, cash, debt, and preferred claims but excludes other liabilities and software value. A 50% Bitcoin drawdown combined with a compression to 0.80× EV/BTC produces a model value near $29 per share. That is an analyst stress scenario, not a liquidation estimate, but it shows why common stock can lose much more than a modest software-revenue miss. [12][13][14]

web_blocks.takeaway: The weighted value is approximately 5.5% below the November 12 close of $114.41. These Bitcoin returns, exit multiples, and probabilities are analyst assumptions—not forecasts. The base case implies 2.71:1 base-target-to-stop asymmetry at the upper $94 support entry, but the current price does not offer the same expected return. [12][13][14]

web_blocks.html: The verdict hinges on one claim: can Strategy turn new capital into positive Bitcoin-per-share yield without exhausting the dollar reserve or depending on a persistent market premium? The falsification test is specific. At the next reported period, Bitcoin Yield should turn positive on the same assumed-diluted-share definition, cash coverage should remain adequate after dividends and interest, and software cash generation should improve rather than rely on financing. If BTC Yield stays negative while preferred obligations and share count rise, the core common-equity rationale weakens even if gross Bitcoin holdings set another record. [1][12][15]

web_blocks.title: New capital and existing shares are different decisions

web_blocks.html: For new capital, the call is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. The November 12 close is not an entry because the stock is far below its 50-day and 200-day averages and the stage classification is unresolved. The review band is $88–$94, around the 63-day base low, with a $79 invalidation. The static-capital base target is $134.64, so the support-zone ratio clears the schema’s 1.5:1 floor; but the band is conditional on a weekly higher low, a break in the sequence of lower lows, and a reclaim of trend measures. A touch alone is not a buy signal. [42][43]

For the current holding, the same-session positions ledger shows 21.414 MSTR shares in Schwab, cost basis $2,699.99, market value $2,449.98, and an unrealized loss of $250.01; the direct position is 2.70% of net worth. The ledger also contains 148.480594 shares of MSTX, a leveraged MSTR vehicle, worth $1,368.99 and 1.51% of net worth. MSTR and MSTX were a 1.00-correlation pair in the position replay, with combined market value of $3,818.97, or 4.21% of net worth. MSTX is not included in the MSTR share count, but it amplifies the same issuer exposure. [45] The scenario model values MSTR at $108.12, 5.5% below the $114.41 close, while the $79 invalidation is 31% below it. We therefore recommend exiting the direct shares at the next available execution opportunity. Re-underwrite MSTX separately; this is not a broker order. [12][42][45]

web_blocks.title: POSITION-RISK DECISION
paragraphs: The direct MSTR shares and MSTX together represent 4.21% of net worth, and the one-year replay shows 1.00 correlation. The below-close expected value and deep invalidation distance do not support retaining the direct MSTR shares. The exit recommendation does not automatically include the separate MSTX fund. [45]

web_blocks.html: Holding action: EXIT_IMMEDIATELY. Exit all 21.414 direct MSTR shares at the next available execution opportunity; the November 12 reference value is $2,449.98, while actual proceeds depend on execution. Reassess the separate MSTX exposure independently. This is advisory, not a broker order. [42][45]

The capital under review includes anticipated proceeds from exiting 21.414 MSTR shares (November 12 reference value $2,449.98; actual proceeds depend on execution), plus the next marginal US cash unit. The active shortlist includes AVPT, whose November 12 snapshot shows a Stage 2 structure, and the outside alternative IBIT offers Bitcoin exposure through a trust with a 0.25% sponsor fee and a November 12 NAV of $40.4352. AVPT has an operating SaaS model and an active shortlist setup; IBIT removes MSTR-specific issuance and preferred-stock risk but still follows Bitcoin without operating cash flow. Neither makes MSTR a better entry today, and the portfolio already has a high effective market exposure. The plan therefore holds 100% in cash until the broad-market correction stabilizes and a current equity setup clears its own business, valuation, and trend gates. [39][42][45]

web_blocks.html: This is an earned wait, not indecision. The operating business has a measurable cloud transition but weak cash sufficiency; the treasury has scale but negative 2026 BTC Yield; the equity is near a short-term support shelf but below its structural trend measures. A new quarterly filing, positive per-share yield, renewed software cash generation, or a durable weekly base would improve the case. A lower BTC price, declining reserve coverage, persistent negative BTC Yield, or a breach of $79 would make it stricter. [1][2][12][15][42]

book_paragraphs: A two-sided review should begin with the best bull case, not a caricature. Strategy holds Bitcoin at a scale few corporate treasuries can approach and has repeatedly accessed common-equity and preferred markets. Its November 8 balances included a $4.77 billion USD Reserve and $146.2 million of USD Cash. Those dollars are not Bitcoin, and that distinction is part of the bull case: a dedicated reserve can pay dividends and interest while limiting the need to sell a volatile asset during a downturn. The company also retains a software operation with a broad installed base and a subscription stream that is growing. [1][2][12]

A bull investor sees a potential capital flywheel. If Bitcoin appreciates, asset coverage grows; if common equity trades above the value of its net Bitcoin and dollar claims, new share issuance can acquire assets without diluting common residual value on the company’s chosen measure. Preferred securities can attract income-seeking capital that might not buy common stock. Repurchases of preferred shares below stated amount may reduce future dividend obligations. The company’s own framework now gives management flexibility among equity issuance, preferred repurchases, reserves, and Bitcoin monetization. This is a real toolkit, but the toolkit only creates value when capital is issued, deployed, and serviced on terms that improve per-share outcomes. [12][13][16][17]

The software option is another legitimate positive. Subscriptions expanded in both the annual and Q3 comparisons, and customers describe the product in consequential workflows: a global field team, a health insurer reducing duplicate reporting, a retailer coordinating pricing and inventory, and a department store using governed AI agents. These examples demonstrate product utility at recognizable organizations. If recurring cloud revenue compounds, implementation becomes repeatable, and customers renew, the software unit could contribute more than its current cash record would suggest. [1][2][5][6][7][8][9]

The strongest bear case does not need to claim that Bitcoin will fail. It can accept that Bitcoin remains a valuable asset and still argue that the MSTR common share is an unstable way to own it. The software operation has not generated positive operating cash in the latest audited year, and management said it would not cover specified obligations or liquidity needs over the next twelve months. Subscription growth is happening while license and support lines fall, and the on-premises support sunset is near. A handful of vendor-published cases do not establish customer retention, customer concentration, or gross-profit durability. [1][2]

The next bear pillar is per-share execution. The corporate objective is explicitly Bitcoin per share, yet the company ledger reports BTC Yield of negative 4.2% year to date through November 9. That measure is designed to include the share denominator. The latest weekly capital allocation makes the distinction concrete: common-stock proceeds were $283.8 million net; $81.9 million went to 1,036 Bitcoin, $188.3 million to STRC repurchases, and $13.6 million to USD Cash. The company may have strengthened its liquidity or capital structure, but the week’s issuance did not all increase Bitcoin holdings. Total BTC is an incomplete proxy for common-shareholder accretion. [12][15]

The preferred layer creates a separate tension. STRC’s annualized dividend rate was 12% on the November 13 product page, but it is variable, subject to monthly adjustment, and not guaranteed. The company says preferred securities are not collateralized by its Bitcoin and have only a preferred claim on residual assets. The policy can broaden demand for income products, but it also creates dollar cash obligations, and the dividend rate is a financing cost rather than free capital. A large reserve buys time; it does not eliminate the need for future capital access or asset monetization. [16][17]

The company’s November 9 capital report demonstrates both adaptation and dependence. Over the latest reported week, it issued 2.05 million MSTR shares for $283.8 million net proceeds, bought back nearly 1.89 million STRC shares for $188.3 million, bought 1,036 Bitcoin for $81.9 million, and added $13.6 million to USD Cash. It also used $21.1 million from the reserve to pay preferred dividends. A bull reads active management and support for digital credit; a bear reads a system whose operations depend on securities issuance and a market in which investors continue to buy several different claims on the same concentrated asset. The same transaction can support both interpretations. [12]

The scenario model is deliberately simple enough for you to audit. Start with 850,364 Bitcoin and a November 12 reference price of $70,822.24; add the disclosed USD Reserve and Cash; subtract debt and estimated preferred notional after the latest reported repurchases; divide by approximate basic-equivalent shares. The base case applies a 15% Bitcoin appreciation and a 1.05× exit enterprise-value-to-Bitcoin ratio, producing $134.64 per share. The bear case combines a 50% Bitcoin loss with 0.80×; the bull case combines 50% Bitcoin growth with 1.20×. None of these outcomes accounts for further dilution, liquidity needs, tax, or software value. [12][13][14]

The weighted expected value is $108.12 with the 40/40/20 probability set, about 5.5% below the current close. The scenario probabilities are not statistical estimates; they are an explicit way to show that a modest base-case gain can coexist with a large left tail. The analyst’s support-zone base-case asymmetry is 2.71:1 at the $94 upper band and $79 stop. That is enough to justify waiting for the price to come to a more favorable zone, but it does not justify buying at $114.41 while the trend remains broken. A new investor can demand both valuation asymmetry and evidence of trend repair. [12][13][14][42]

The hinge is the per-share metric, not the number of coins purchased in any one week. If future filings show positive BTC Yield, a stable or increasing coverage reserve, and an improving software cash profile, the bull case gains support. If BTC Yield stays negative while preferred claims and shares continue to expand, then the assertion that the financing system compounds for common shareholders is falsified even if headline Bitcoin holdings keep rising. You can test this through the company’s own defined KPI and its share-count schedule instead of debating slogans. [1][12][15]

For the direct MSTR holding, the account record shows 21.414 shares in Schwab with $2,699.99 cost and $2,449.98 market value, a $250.01 unrealized loss and 2.70% portfolio weight. The account also owns 148.480594 shares of MSTX worth $1,368.99. The one-year holdings replay shows a 1.00 correlation, making the combined direct market value about 4.21% of net worth. This is meaningful linked exposure, though MSTX remains a separate leveraged product. [45]

The position decision is to exit all 21.414 direct MSTR shares at the next available execution opportunity. The model’s $108.12 probability-weighted value is below the $114.41 close, and the $79 invalidation lies about 31% below that reference price. At the November 12 close, the position was worth $2,449.98; actual sale proceeds may differ. This recommendation does not automatically include MSTX, which is a separate leveraged fund and needs its own review. The exit is advisory, not a broker instruction. [12][42][45]

For new capital, the next marginal cash unit remains in cash. AVPT is the active shortlist comparator; its 12 November close was $16.38 and its current underwriting shows a $22.80 base target, but the broad market is still in Correction and the current dossier’s capital review does not need to add another high-beta software position. IBIT is the outside alternative: it held spot Bitcoin, reported a November 12 NAV of $40.4352 and closing price of $40.36, and charged a 0.25% sponsor fee. It removes MSTR’s preferred-stock and share-premium machinery while retaining direct Bitcoin price risk and charging an ongoing fee. Neither receives an allocation in this plan until its own entry, portfolio-risk, and market-context gates are rechecked. [39][42][45]

The final judgment is therefore conditional by horizon. Short term, do not chase: the chart is below its structural averages, the options engine finds no edge, and the market backdrop is corrective. Medium term, monitor cloud subscription growth, cash conversion, reserve coverage, preferred costs, and positive BTC Yield. Long term, Strategy may still be an innovative way to engineer Bitcoin exposure, but it has not yet demonstrated that gross holdings translate into positive per-share compounding through a weak capital market. The current evidence earns a wait-for-support call, not an unconditional endorsement or an automatic rejection. [1][2][12][15][42]

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR’S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Keep the bull’s real strengths: asset scale, financing flexibility, a cloud transition, and a large reserve. Keep the bear’s real warning: per-share Bitcoin yield is negative, software cash is insufficient, and the shares remain below trend. The verdict should change only when the evidence changes. [1][2][12][15]

book_callouts.title: Decision rule
book_callouts.text: Exit the direct MSTR shares at the next available execution opportunity and keep the proceeds in cash. Review the separate MSTX position on its own; the conditional $88–$94 band and $79 invalidation apply only to any future MSTR entry. [42][45]
